# TravelProof

**Prove the counterparty was screened. Keep who they are off the ledger.**

_BLI Legal Tech Hackathon 2 · LegalTech / RegTech track · Chainlink CRE bounty_

## The Problem

When one exchange sends crypto to another, the FATF Travel Rule (Recommendation 16) and the EU Transfer of Funds Regulation make the originating VASP screen the counterparty and transmit originator and beneficiary information. Put that information on a public chain and you leak personal data, the exact harm data-protection law exists to stop. The compliance officer owes two duties at once: prove the screen happened, and never expose who was screened. The rule also branches: exchange-to-exchange, exchange-to-self-custody, and sub-threshold transfers each trigger a different regime and a different citation.

## What We Built

TravelProof separates the proof from the identity. A deterministic resolver classifies the transfer and its governing regime (no language model decides a verdict). A Chainlink CRE verify workflow checks IVMS101 identity off-chain; a CRE screen workflow runs a DON-consensus OFAC SDN check against the live Treasury feed, fail-closed. Only a one-way `keccak256` commitment, two verdict enums, and a timestamp reach the chain, carried by a DON-signed attestation on `TravelRuleAttestation` (Base Sepolia). The officer gets a filable transmittal record and a cited one-page memo; an examiner reads `/ledger` and sees that screening happened, not who was screened.

## Our Chainlink CRE Integration

- **Verify workflow** (`packages/cre/cre-run/verify/main.ts`): POSTs the IVMS payload to a bearer-gated endpoint doing a real TRISA testnet directory lookup; emits a commitment, not identity.
- **Screen workflow** (`packages/cre/cre-run/screen/main.ts`): DON-consensus OFAC SDN screen against the live feed, via a tiny `GET /api/ofac?address=` endpoint so the in-workflow fetch stays inside the CRE HTTP capability limit.
- **Attestation** (`contracts/src/TravelRuleAttestation.sol`): `onReport` decodes KeystoneForwarder metadata, binds the expected workflow, reverts `UnexpectedWorkflow` otherwise. The stored struct has no string fields.

Both workflows compile against `@chainlink/cre-sdk` 1.23.0 and run end-to-end via local CRE simulation (no beta): `/api/run` returns a real `CLEARED` or `DO NOT TRANSMIT`. See the [repo README](https://github.com/dmustapha/travelproof/blob/main/README.md) for the full architecture, the security table, and deployed-contract detail.

## What Makes This Different

A fabricated verdict is structurally impossible: an unavailable or non-enum CRE result returns `502`, never a faked `CLEARED`. PII on-chain is structurally impossible: the `Attestation` struct carries no string field, so a name cannot be stored. The classifier encodes the statute (FATF R.16, EU TFR Art.14, de-minimis divergence), not a single hard-coded case.

## Verify in 60s

A cold reviewer can re-derive the core engine from a fresh clone, no wallet and no keys:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dmustapha/travelproof && cd travelproof
pnpm install
pnpm verify:claims   # recomputes every commitment from committed source; non-zero exit on any mismatch
pnpm -r test         # deterministic resolver + outcome truth-table + chain read path
```

What you watch re-derive: the commitment the verify workflow serializes on-chain is recomputed from committed source and compared, and the outcome truth-table proves each regime branch (FATF R.16 vs EU TFR Art.14 vs de-minimis) returns the correct citation and action. The OFAC screen is live: `curl "https://travelproof.vercel.app/api/ofac?address=3Lpoy53K625zVeE47ZasiG5jGkAxJ27kh1"` returns `{"hit":true}` for the Garantex SDN address. Weaker-but-visible: open https://travelproof.vercel.app and run a transfer.

## Try It

1. Open https://travelproof.vercel.app.
2. Submit a transfer intent in the cockpit; watch the classifier pick the regime and citation.
3. See the record render with the commitment, verdicts, and (on a live-CRE host) the attestation reference, plus the examiner log at `/ledger`.

## Demo Notes (Real / Simulated / Beta)

- **Real:** the deployed contract, the OFAC SDN live-feed screen (the Garantex hit flips the verdict), the TRISA testnet directory registration lookup, the deterministic classifier, the IVMS101 record, the memo, the examiner ledger, the 101/101 stress battery.
- **Local CRE simulation:** verify and screen verdicts come from `cre workflow simulate` (DON and enclave emulated on the host, real data, a real DON-signed report in simulation). This needs no beta.
- **Beta-gated:** the production managed-DON confidential enclave, and broadcasting the simulated attestation on-chain, both need Chainlink's Confidential Workflows beta. On the public Vercel instance the full managed-DON path fails closed and a verdict there is labelled `SPECIMEN`.
